note: 24 Gated-DeltaNet layers + 8 full-attention layers. UNLIKE qwen3.5-0.8b/2b, the GDN key and value head counts are DECOUPLED (16 key heads, 32 value heads) — Q/K are broadcast (repeat_interleave) up to the value head count before the recurrence; V is already at 32. State tensor is [32,128,128], not [16,128,128]. NOT an official OE-LLM architecture; BLLM-native only. The vision half of the checkpoint is dropped for the text package (see the qwen3.5-vlm recipe).

quantisation.kept_fp32: SSM recurrence, depthwise conv, RMSNorms, GDN gated-norm
quantisation.note: Flat +-32/+-64 activation ranges clip this size's deep linears (measured max|input| ~198 on 'down', ~84 on q/k/v, ~65 on the GDN gates) into a degenerate loop. Calibration: max|input| * 1.3 margin from a real fp32 decode forward over a small prompt set, recorded per linear.

variants.name: qwen3.5-4b-ctx4k-int8-s100
variants.prefill: chunked-float-N32; head-splitting adapted for the decoupled GDN heads, chunked-delta-rule math itself unchanged from qwen3.5-0.8b/2b (see README). This release also rewrites attention from expand_win broadcast to GQA batched matmul + mask deduplication, ported down from qwen3.5-0.8b — SEE CAVEAT below, this is the one variant in the family where that rewrite is not a pure no-op.

toolchain.note: Recorded so a future regression can be attributed. Host toolchain and board HBRT must match.

measured.note:
Re-measured S100P, 2026-07-29, performance mode set, against the current GQA+mask-dedup build (common/bench_vlm.py, 3 repeated chat() runs with a real image, temp=0). decode_tok_s is 6.14, nearly 2x the pre-rewrite baseline's 3.29 — the GQA batched matmul drops most of the expand_win broadcast's redundant DMA. bpu_graph_ms and effective_weight_bandwidth_GBps below are DERIVED (scaled from the pre-rewrite values by the decode_tok_s ratio, 6.14/3.29 = 1.87x) — NOT independently re-measured via hrt_model_exec this pass; treat as an estimate, not a hardware profile.

CAVEAT (unlike 0.8b/2b, where the GQA rewrite reproduces the prior build's output bit-for-bit): 4B's original expand_win attention had NO int16 quantisation on the attention score/output matmul; the ported GQA path wraps that matmul in int16 like 0.8b/2b already did, since it reuses their code path. Board output after the rewrite is NOT byte-identical to the pre-rewrite baseline (e.g. one prior answer mentioned 'one adult and one cub', the new build's phrasing omits that detail) — verified this is a real, expected precision perturbation from the newly-added quantisation, not a bug: the batched-matmul math itself was checked algebraically exact against the old expand_win math offline (numpy, exact 4B head config NHa=16/NKV=4/HDa=256/REP=4/CL=4096, cosine 1.0000001, max abs diff 2.38e-7). This release's formal acceptance run (parity/ppl/image-contrast/anchors, all below) is what actually clears this build for use, not the offline math check alone — a build can be algebraically exact and still misbehave downstream, so the two aren't a substitute for each other.

ppl.measured: S100P, 2026-07-29, common/eval_ppl.py against the GQA+mask-dedup build

task_metric.name: coherence-anchors + prefill/decode parity + image contrast
task_metric.protocol: common/eval_parity.py (prefill vs no-prefill, text-mode session on the same .hbm) — first-token match, 48-token greedy identical, control-ppl identical; with-image vs without-image contrast on a real photo (two brown bears), temp=0; EN factual, ZH factual, arithmetic; multi-turn name recall
task_metric.measured: pass — parity PASS (S100P, 2026-07-29, first-token match + 48-token greedy identical + control-ppl identical — this passing despite the CAVEAT above because parity compares the new build against ITSELF with/without the prefill graph, not against the old pre-rewrite build); image contrast PASS (correctly identifies two brown bears / grizzly subspecies with image, correctly declines without); EN/ZH/arithmetic anchors PASS; multi-turn memory correct (verified via the model's own visible reasoning trace, same thinking-mode-truncation caveat as qwen3.5-2b)

task_metric.measured: pass — parity PASS, image contrast PASS (same photo, equivalent answer to ctx4k), EN/ZH/arithmetic PASS, multi-turn memory correct (same thinking-mode-truncation caveat)

rejected_builds.name: flat int16 activation ranges (copied from 0.8b/2b)
rejected_builds.why: The flat +-32/+-64 ranges that fit 0.8b/2b clip this size's deep linears (real max|input| up to ~198 vs the +-64 range on 'down') into a degenerate loop. The build compiles and runs fluently — it just answers wrong. Fixed by per-linear calibration; see README.

rejected_builds.name: symmetric GDN head split (copied from 0.8b/2b prefill recipe without adapting for decoupled heads)
rejected_builds.why: This model's checkpoint has linear_num_key_heads=16, linear_num_value_heads=32 (vs 16/16 on the smaller siblings). A prefill graph ported from a symmetric sibling without inserting the Q/K broadcast-to-value-head-count step, and without moving the tensor split boundaries to be key-head-width for Q/K and value-head-width for V, does not match the checkpoint's actual weight shapes.

rejected_builds.name: block_quantized_matmul (dynamic-quant decode)
rejected_builds.why: Same failure as qwen3.5-0.8b: the dynamic per-token quant path is a PREFILL op, ~130x slower per matmul in decode.

rejected_builds.name: all-BPU chunked prefill (Newton triangular inverse)
rejected_builds.why: Same numerical failure as qwen3.5-0.8b — not re-derived at this size, the mechanism is head-count independent.

board_verification.flow: stop resident serving processes; run common/eval_parity.py + common/eval_ppl.py against a text-mode view of the package (same model.hbm/model_prefill.hbm, model.json with the visual key dropped — the decoder graph is unchanged by adding vision, see qwen3.5-vlm recipe); run image-contrast + task-coherence anchors through the actual NativeVlmSession; benchmark decode_tok_s/ttft_ms via common/bench_vlm.py; restore the stopped processes
